messages:
paul: Quick sync — we need a final decision on the canonical error payload + HTTP status mapping for chat, embeddings, and rerank before we freeze launch criteria. Main concerns: retry semantics, streaming errors, and guidance for SDKs.

denise: +1. we should separate user-facing HTTP status (429/422/503/500/403) from internal error codes that signal automations (e.g. MODEL_UNAVAILABLE).

mike: Agreed. Proposal from platform: keep short http codes and a structured body with `code` (string), `message` (string), and optional `details` (array). SDKs should surface code + retry_after when present.

katy: Can we include `retry_after_ms` in all rate-limit responses and `retry_after_ms` for model-unavailable when we expect a transient recovery? That makes client behaviour deterministic.

paul: yes — customer asks specifically require deterministic guidance. Also need explicit behavior for streaming endpoints (chat). If model fails mid-stream, what do we return?

denise: For streaming: close stream with an `event: error` chunk that contains the same structured payload. Example: 

```
> event: error
> data: {"code":"MODEL_UNAVAILABLE","message":"primary-gpu OOM; falling back","retry_after_ms":12000,"hint":"fallback:small-quant"}
```

denise: That lets clients decide to retry, show partial output, or fall back.

ryan: From CS: customers want a clear difference between validation (bad request) vs. rate vs. soft model failures. They expect 422 for prompt/schema validation with a field-level path.

ali: For embeddings and rerank, validation errors are common. Suggest 422 with `field_errors`: e.g. `[{"path":"input[2]","message":"exceeds max tokens"}]`. Keep the top-level message concise.

mike: OK. Draft mapping: 
- 400: malformed JSON / invalid media type
- 401/403: auth/forbidden
- 422: validation (body semantics) with `field_errors`
- 429: rate limit (include `quota_pool` and `retry_after_ms`)
- 503: service degraded (use `code` values MODEL_UNAVAILABLE, CAPACITY_EXCEEDED)
- 500: unexpected internal error (include `incident_id`)

paul: Nice. What about a retry header vs. body? platform folks prefer `Retry-After` header for caches, but SDKs might prefer body. We probably need both for robustness.

mike: We'll emit standard `Retry-After` (seconds) header on 429/503 and also `retry_after_ms` in JSON where we can compute more precise timing.

katy: SDK semantics: automatic retries only on 429 and MODEL_UNAVAILABLE when `retry_after_ms` present and < 30s. Otherwise surface the error to the app. We'll document idempotency guidance per endpoint.

denise: Rerank/nondeterministic endpoints: recommend clients treat generate/rerank as non-idempotent unless they pass an `idempotency_key`. For retriable model-unavailable we still gate auto-retry behind idempotency_key to avoid duplicates.

ryan: Customers asked for a `fallback_suggestion` in the payload when we can auto-route to a cheaper/quantized variant. e.g. `"fallback_hint":"gpt-small-quant"`. Good or nah?

ali: Fine as a hint only. Should not be actionable for compliance customers. Add `fallback_allowed` boolean so Private customers can opt-out.

paul: Good — add to open items. Also need consistent `client_action` enum to guide SDKs/apps (values: SHOW_ERROR, RETRY_AFTER, USE_FALLBACK, USE_PARTIAL).

mike: I'll add `client_action` to the example payloads. Example response for rate limit: 

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 15

{
  "code": "RATE_LIMIT",
  "message": "requests per-minute exceeded",
  "retry_after_ms": 15000,
  "quota_pool": "user:uploads",
  "client_action": "RETRY_AFTER"
}
```

mike: Example for model unavailable with fallback hint: 

```
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
Retry-After: 12

{
  "code": "MODEL_UNAVAILABLE",
  "message": "primary region GPUs busy",
  "retry_after_ms": 12000,
  "client_action": "USE_FALLBACK",
  "fallback_hint": "gpt-compat-small-quant",
  "fallback_allowed": true
}
```

katy: For validation: 
```
HTTP/1.1 422 Unprocessable Entity
{
  "code": "VALIDATION_ERROR",
  "message": "input schema invalid",
  "field_errors": [{"path":"input[0].text","message":"exceeds 8k token limit"}],
  "client_action": "SHOW_ERROR"
}
```

denise: We also need an internal canonical code namespace (string) documented in the API spec so SDKs can handle without brittle string-matching. We'll publish a mapping table in the launch docs.

paul: Launch gating: product wants docs + SDK behavior + e2e tests that assert a) correct headers, b) structured payload fields present, c) streaming error event format. Engineering: are these feasible for next release?

mike: Yes but need 2 sprints to implement header+body parity across all endpoints and tests. Streaming error event will require updates to our stream broker.

denise: Also require a small compatibility shim: older clients (pre-1.3 SDK) should still get plain text 503/429; new clients get structured JSON when they send `Accept: application/json` or `X-Client-Version: >=1.3`.

ryan: Make sure CS gets a migration note; we'll have some customers on old SDKs.

paul: Action items: 
- mike: implement HTTP header + structured body for 429/503/422/500 (owner)
- denise: stream error event format + backward compatibility plan (owner)
- katy: write SDK retry semantics doc + sample code (owner)
- ali: add field_errors format for embeddings/rerank test prompts (owner)
- ryan: prepare customer comms + migration playbook (owner)

paul: Let's reconvene in 48h with a PR that includes sample payloads and a short compatibility matrix. If no blockers, we'll add this to the API launch criteria checklist. :white_check_mark:

infra-bot: deploy-bot: scheduled a patch branch build to validate 429/503 headers on staging at 2026-08-03T09:10Z (build 3821).

mike: noted. I'll align tests to that build and ping when green.

paul: thanks all — filing follow-ups in the API spec doc after this thread.
